candidates.name: TapTable
candidates.rationale: Two of the most literal words in the category, in the order the action happens: the card lands on the table, the guest taps. Reads naturally next to 'Tap to review' and a server can say 'drop the TapTable card' without stumbling. Note: I could not run live collision checks (session search budget exhausted); 'TapTable' is generic enough that a POS or ordering product may already use it, so verify USPTO and app stores before committing.
candidates.tagline: Reviews, one tap from the table.
candidates.conflicts: TapTable (UK) — contactless/NFC+QR order-and-pay app for restaurants and bars, active since ~2020 (Instagram @taptableuk; https://www.f6s.com/company/taptableapp; Devpost hackathon entry also named TapTable for QR/NFC restaurant ordering). Also 'Taptable' restaurant/club reservation app. taptable.com registered 2008 but currently shows an empty page.

candidates.name: TableStars
candidates.rationale: 'Stars' is the universal shorthand for a rating, and 'table' anchors it in dine-in restaurants specifically. The AI report can be positioned as 'your stars, explained.' No known conflict with a review/NFC company from memory, but it is a plausible restaurant-award or reservation brand name, so check.
candidates.tagline: Every table, five stars closer.
candidates.conflicts: No tech/review-software conflicts found. Only hits: 'Tablestars' a small business listing in Palm Harbor FL (MapQuest), and 'Table Stars' a Dutch youth table-tennis program (tafeltennis.nl). tablestars.com (GoDaddy, 2015) does not resolve to a live site.

candidates.name: CheckTap
candidates.rationale: Plays on the restaurant 'check' (the bill) and the moment the card is dropped with it, plus 'tap.' Distinctive enough to own; two hard consonants make it crisp on a card. Low risk of collision with major review/NFC players from memory, but verify.
candidates.tagline: Drop the check. Collect the review.
candidates.conflicts: Checktap — defunct South Korean smart power-strip maker (https://tracxn.com, 'deadpooled'), plus a dormant UK shell 'Checktap Limited' (Companies House). Neither in restaurant/review tech. checktap.com is a GoDaddy for-sale parked page. Note: name is a near-reversal of Tapcheck (registered TM, see below), which could cause confusion.

candidates.name: GuestTap
candidates.rationale: 'Guest' is hospitality's own word for a customer, signaling the founder understands the industry; 'tap' is the action. Reads well beside 'Tap to review' and is easy for staff to say. 'GuestTap'-style names are common in hospitality tech (guest Wi-Fi, guest messaging), so a trademark search is essential.
candidates.tagline: Turn every guest into a review.
candidates.conflicts: No company found. 'Guest tap' is a common craft-brewery term (a tap pouring another brewery's beer; #guesttap hashtag widely used), which muddies search results and SEO for bars/breweries. guesttap.com is parked for sale on HugeDomains.

candidates.name: RateCard
candidates.rationale: A real English compound with a second meaning (a rate card is a price list), which makes it memorable and instantly describes a card you use to rate. Card-first naming fits Product 1 exactly. 'Rate card' is a generic term, so the .com is likely taken or expensive; check alternates.
candidates.tagline: The card that asks the question.
candidates.conflicts: Ratecard — established feedback & reviews SaaS for HR/recruiting/staffing (https://get.ratecard.io, ratecard.com; listed on software review sites). Same name, same category (collecting reviews/feedback). Also 'rate card' is a generic advertising-pricing term.

candidates.name: StarDrop
candidates.rationale: 'Drop' is literally what the server does with the card ('drop the StarDrop card' rolls off the tongue), and 'star' says rating. Short, energetic, and friendlier than most B2B names. From memory there is no major review-tech company under this name, but the word pair is popular in gaming and fashion, so check classes carefully.
candidates.tagline: Drop the card. Catch the stars.
candidates.conflicts: Stardrop — popular open-source Stardew Valley mod manager (https://github.com/Floogen/Stardrop) dominates search; not a business competitor but owns the name's search results. StarDrop is also a Stardew Valley in-game item (Stardrop trademark context via ConcernedApe). stardrop.com (1999, Japanese registrar) no live site; stardrop.co parked for sale on GoDaddy.

candidates.name: TipStar
candidates.rationale: Bridges the two things a guest does at the end of a meal: leave a tip and (now) leave a star. Servers will like saying it because it associates reviews with tips. Warning: 'tip' could be read as a tipping product; the tagline and card copy need to keep it clearly about reviews. Verify no fintech/tipping app uses it.
candidates.tagline: Leave a star with your tip.
candidates.conflicts: TIPSTAR — major Japanese betting/keirin streaming app (https://tipstar.com, registered via MarkMonitor = corporate brand protection, likely trademarked). Tipstar — football-betting predictions app on App Store/Google Play (Squidbay Srl). Gambling associations are a poor fit for a restaurant tipping/review brand.

candidates.name: ReviewDrop
candidates.rationale: Fully descriptive: the card is dropped, the review is collected. 'Drop the ReviewDrop card' is redundant but clear; staff will simply say 'drop the ReviewDrop.' Works well for the monthly report too ('your monthly ReviewDrop'). Generic construction means the .com may be held; check alternates.
candidates.tagline: One drop. Every review.
candidates.conflicts: Reviewdrop — review collection/widget SaaS (https://reviewdrop.io; Crunchbase profile) AND a second ReviewDrop at https://www.reviewdrop.app that auto-sends review requests from QuickBooks invoices. Two active same-name review-software products. reviewdrop.com is parked for sale on GoDaddy.

candidates.name: TapStars
candidates.rationale: Instantly understood: tap, get stars. Reads as a natural caption under the phone-tap icon on the card face. Simple plural gives it a friendlier, consumer-facing tone that makes guests more likely to engage. Highly generic, so expect trademark neighbors in mobile games and rating apps; verify.
candidates.tagline: Tap once. Shine on Google.
candidates.conflicts: Direct competitors with identical name and product: TapStars (France, https://tapstars.com) sells NFC plaques for Google reviews at checkout to retail/hospitality; Tapstars (Australia, https://tapstars.com.au, Instagram @_tapstars_) sells NFC Google review cards; also 'Tap Star' NFC Google review cards Australia (tapstar.com.au). Same product category as yours.

candidates.name: GuestVoice
candidates.rationale: Shifts emphasis from the mechanism (tap) to the outcome (hearing from guests), which also sells the AI report: every month the restaurant gets the voice of its guests summarized. Sounds established and trustworthy to a 55-year-old owner. Enterprise 'voice of customer' vendors exist, so verify there is no direct hospitality conflict.
candidates.tagline: Hear what every table is saying.
candidates.conflicts: Crowded: GuestVoice (https://guestvoice.app) table-QR private feedback + Google review prompts for restaurants (nearly identical product); GuestVoice (https://guestvoice.net) table-QR guest experience for hotels/restaurants; GuestVoice (https://guestvoice.space) complaint capture before bad reviews; Guest Voice AI (https://guestvoice.ai) hotel messaging; GuestVoice is also Marriott's Medallia-powered guest feedback program. guestvoice.com parked on HugeDomains.

candidates.name: TableTalk
candidates.rationale: A real idiom for candid conversation over a meal, repurposed to mean reviews from the table plus the monthly report that 'talks back' with insights. Warm and very pronounceable. Known downside: it is a common phrase, so expect existing podcasts, restaurants and possibly a reservation/marketing product; the .com is almost certainly taken.
candidates.tagline: What your guests say when they leave the table.
candidates.conflicts: Very common name: Tabletalk Magazine (Ligonier Ministries, tabletalkmagazine.com), TableTalk 'Join the Conversation' (https://www.tabletalk.com), Tabletalk web app (https://www.tabletalk.co), Table Talk SA news (tabletalk.co.za), Table Talk Online, plus a well-known Table Talk pies brand. All three candidate domains are taken.

candidates.name: FiveTap
candidates.rationale: 'Five' evokes five stars without saying it, and 'tap' is the action. Short, numeric names are easy to remember and stand out on a small card. 'Drop the FiveTap card' is smooth. Low collision risk in review tech from memory, though a similar-sounding brand (e.g., 'Five Star' variants) could argue confusion; verify.
candidates.tagline: Five stars, one tap.
candidates.conflicts: FiveTap (https://fivetap.net) — 'Tap in, walk out booked': NFC tap tags on chairs/mirrors linking to booking page, reviews, and socials for salons/service businesses. Same NFC tap-for-reviews concept, adjacent vertical. fivetap.io also has DNS. fivetap.com parked for sale on HugeDomains.

candidates.name: TapCheck
candidates.rationale: Mirror of CheckTap, with 'tap' first so it echoes the card's 'Tap to review' instruction. Doubles as 'check in on your reviews' for the report. Caution: I recall a workforce/payroll app called Tapcheck; if that is confirmed, prefer CheckTap instead.
candidates.tagline: Tap here. Your review counts.
candidates.conflicts: Tapcheck® — large, well-funded earned-wage-access/on-demand pay company with a registered trademark (https://www.tapcheck.com), integrated with ADP, heavily used by restaurant/hospitality employers. Payments/fintech adjacency makes trademark confusion very likely. All three domains taken (tapcheck.co parked on GoDaddy).

candidates.name: TapToRate
candidates.rationale: The most literal option in the set: it is the instruction itself. Works as brand, card copy and call to action at once, which keeps the card face uncluttered. Highly descriptive names are harder to trademark and 'tap to rate' products likely exist on marketplaces, so this is best as a fallback or as a card headline under another brand.
candidates.tagline: Tap to rate. That's the whole job.
candidates.conflicts: taptorate (https://taptorate.co, registered Jul 2026) — 'Premium NFC review cards for local businesses... tap their phone and your Google review page opens instantly'; identical product. 'Tap to Rate' is also a generic descriptor used on Temu/Etsy NFC review card listings, so it is weak as a trademark. taptorate.com (2011) has no live site.

candidates.name: Clink
candidates.rationale: The sound of glasses touching and the sound of a card tapping a phone in one five-letter real word. Instantly restaurant-native, verb-ready ("clink it before you leave"), and reads cleanly next to "Tap to review". Domain reality: clink.com (registered 1997), getclink.com (2022) and clinkcards.com (2026-05-08) are all taken per Verisign WHOIS on 2026-09-04, and clink.io has been registered since 2017 (whois.nic.io). Strong name, weak domain position; expect to buy a modifier domain such as clinkreviews.com or clinktap.com. No NFC/review-tech company named Clink was found, but the name is generic enough that a trademark search is essential.
candidates.tagline: Clink. Tap. Reviewed.
taken_domains: clinkreviews.com (reg. Oct 2025, Eranet, no live site)
clinktap.com (reg. Apr 2025, Realtime Register, no live site)
candidates.conflicts: Crowded name. Clink 360-degree feedback/business software listed on SourceForge/Slashdot (https://sourceforge.net/software/product/Clink, https://slashdot.org/software/Clink); 'Clink' platform on LinkedIn (https://www.linkedin.com/company/joinclinkplatform); Clink dating app and Clink Smart Home app on App Store/Google Play (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/clink, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.noid.clink); useclink.app, clink-it.app, clink.glass; Clink! restaurants in Boston (https://clinkboston.com) and Salem OR. Notably clinkreviews.com and clinktap.com were both registered by third parties in 2025, suggesting someone else may be building a 'Clink' review/tap product.

candidates.name: Huzzah
candidates.rationale: An old-fashioned cheer that feels celebratory and slightly playful, which fits a card handed over at the happiest moment of a meal. Six letters, unmistakable pronunciation, memorable for servers ("drop the Huzzah card"). Verisign WHOIS on 2026-09-04: huzzah.com registered since 1996 and gethuzzah.com since 2013, but huzzahcards.com returned No match (unregistered). huzzah.io registered since 2014 per whois.nic.io. No review or NFC company using the name was found in checks.
candidates.tagline: Give your guests a reason to cheer. Out loud, on Google.
taken_domains: huzzah.com (reg. 1996, MarkMonitor - corporate brand protection registrar)
candidates.conflicts: Huzzah Media (https://huzzahmedia.com) sells a customer loyalty platform and mobile apps to small businesses, plus 'Huzzah Loyalty Rewards' app (https://apkpure.com/huzzah-loyalty-rewards/com.huzzah.customer) - adjacent to restaurant/local-business tech. Also huzzah.food, huzzah.app, Huzzah event planning app (https://apps.apple.com/za/app/huzzah), huzzah! digital agency, Huzzah Performing Arts, huzzahwin.com gambling site.

candidates.name: Kudoz
candidates.rationale: Kudos with a Z: the word literally means praise, and the altered spelling makes it ownable and trademark-friendly in the Popl/Blinq tradition. Five letters, one syllable pair, easy to say. Domain reality per Verisign WHOIS on 2026-09-04: kudoz.com registered 2002 (currently serves an empty 114-byte page), getkudoz.com registered 2026-02-09 and is listed for sale, and kudozcards.com was registered 2025-09-23 by someone else (returned no content when fetched) - that last one is a yellow flag that another party may be moving on this name in the cards space. kudoz.io registered 2020.
candidates.tagline: Kudoz: praise your guests were already thinking.
candidates.conflicts: DIRECT COMPETITOR. Kudoz Reviews (https://www.kudozreviews.com, https://apps.apple.com/us/app/kudoz-reviews, https://www.g2.com/products/kudoz-reviews/reviews) is a reputation-management platform for local businesses including restaurants, sells 'Kudoz Tap Cards' (NFC tap-to-review), smart review routing, $199/mo, 5.0 on G2/Capterra, LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/kudoz-reviews. kudozcards.com is already taken (likely by them). Also kudoz.io, kudoz.to, kudoz.ca. Do not use.

candidates.name: Bravvo
candidates.rationale: Bravo is what you shout after a great performance, and a great meal is a performance. The doubled V makes it coined and searchable. Six letters, reads well on a card. Collision note: bravvo.com (registered 2007) is a live site for virtual fitness medal challenges (page title "Bravvo | Earn Your Medals with Our Virtual Challenges", fetched 2026-09-04), and getbravvo.com was registered 2025-12-01. That is an unrelated category, but it means the .com is gone. bravvocards.com returned No match (unregistered) per Verisign WHOIS on 2026-09-04. bravvo.io registered 2020.
candidates.tagline: Every great meal deserves a Bravvo.
taken_domains: bravvo.co (reg. 2026-09-03, one day before this check, Spaceship)
bravvo.app (registered via OVH, resolves to 213.186.33.5, no live site)
candidates.conflicts: Bravvo fitness challenges/medals app (https://www.bravvo.com, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bravvo.app, Trustpilot 4 stars); Bravvo.io employee engagement/sustainability B2B platform (https://app.bravvo.io, https://www.f6s.com/software/bravvo); Bravvo Inc registered in PA. Neither is in restaurant/review tech, but 'Bravvo' is also easily confused with Bravo (NBC app, Bravo HR app). bravvo.co being registered yesterday suggests someone else is actively pursuing this name.

candidates.name: Plaudo
candidates.rationale: From plaudit and applaud, with a Latin-flavored -o ending that sounds like a real word without being one. Six letters, two syllables, no spelling ambiguity once heard. Cleanest domain position of the applause family: plaudo.com is registered (2005) but currently serves an empty 114-byte page, while getplaudo.com and plaudocards.com both returned No match (unregistered) and plaudo.io returned Domain not found, all per registry WHOIS on 2026-09-04. No company named Plaudo was found in checks. Note: Plaud (no O) is an existing AI voice-recorder brand, so keep the O prominent in logo and speech.
candidates.tagline: Plaudo turns a good dinner into a Google review.
candidates.conflicts: No company called 'Plaudo' in tech; only PLAUDO LLC in Webster MA (2005 filing, https://www.bizapedia.com/ma/plaudo-llc.html) and a Spotify artist PLAUDO (169K monthly listeners). Main concern is Plaud.ai (https://www.plaud.ai), a large AI note-taking/summary brand with 2M+ users - 'Plaudo' is one letter away and both involve AI summaries, so search results for Plaudo are dominated by Plaud.

candidates.name: Regale
candidates.rationale: A real word with a double meaning that is perfect for restaurants: to regale is to entertain lavishly with food and drink, and also to tell someone a story. The card asks guests to regale the world with what they just ate. Six letters, familiar, upscale. Verisign WHOIS on 2026-09-04: regale.com registered since 1999 and getregale.com since 2025-03-18, but regalecards.com returned No match (unregistered). regale.io registered 2020 per whois.nic.io. No review or NFC company found under the name.
candidates.tagline: Regale: let your guests tell the story.
taken_domains: regale.co (reg. 2019, InternetX, currently clientHold/autoRenewPeriod - registered but on hold, may drop)
candidates.conflicts: Regale is a REGISTERED TRADEMARK of 3Sharp LLC for a B2B demo/sales SaaS platform (https://www.regale.cloud, Capterra https://www.capterra.com/p/Regale, listed on GetApp/Slashdot). Also a 'Regale' AI biographer iPhone app (https://appshunter.io/ios/app/regale-chronicle-your-odyssey) and confusion with Regal Cinemas app. Registered software trademark makes this risky for a SaaS product.

candidates.name: Lauda
candidates.rationale: Latin root laudare, to praise (the root of applaud and laudable). Five letters, soft vowels, sounds like a premium hospitality brand rather than a gadget. Good for a logo on a dark card. Domain position per Verisign WHOIS on 2026-09-04: lauda.com registered since 1996, but getlauda.com and laudacards.com both returned No match (unregistered). lauda.io registered 2020. Association risk: Niki Lauda is a famous racing name, and Lauda is also an Austrian airline brand, so a trademark search in class 9/35/42 is required before committing.
candidates.tagline: Lauda. Praise, captured at the table.
candidates.conflicts: LAUDA Dr. R. Wobser GmbH, a German lab temperature-control company with 'Lauda App' on App Store/Google Play (https://www.lauda.de, https://apps.apple.com/us/app/lauda-app); Lauda Europe / Laudamotion airline (Ryanair subsidiary, https://www.trustpilot.com/review/laudamotion.com); lauda.app exists; Niki Lauda name recognition; Lauda Leadership Dynamics at lauda.com. None in restaurant/review tech but the name is heavily used and search-dominated by others.

candidates.name: Hoorah
candidates.rationale: A cheer with more warmth than Huzzah and a spelling that avoids the military hooah/oorah associations. Six letters, easy for any server to say, and it works as a verb ("hoorah your guests"). Best raw domain availability on the list among cheer words: hoorah.com registered 2003, but gethoorah.com and hoorahcards.com both returned No match (unregistered) per Verisign WHOIS on 2026-09-04. hoorah.io registered 2016. No review-tech company found under the name.
candidates.tagline: Hoorah: the review that happens before the check.
candidates.conflicts: 'Hoorah - Rating For All' iOS app is a platform for rating anything (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hoorah-rating-for-all) - same review/rating space, though it is a consumer social app of Chinese origin with only 5 ratings. Also Hoorah Tickets (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/hoorahtickets.com), Hoorah prop-trading firm (https://www.myfxbook.com/reviews/prop-trading-firms/hoorah), hoorah.games, shoorah.io. Common military-slang word, weak trademark.

candidates.name: Praisd
candidates.rationale: Dropped-vowel spelling of praised, in the Blinq/Tumblr tradition. Six letters, one syllable, and it describes the outcome for the restaurant: you got praised. Reads well small. Domain reality per Verisign WHOIS on 2026-09-04: praisd.com was registered 2026-02-23 and currently hosts a password-gated private members-only shop (fetched 2026-09-04) that has nothing to do with reviews, NFC, or restaurants. getpraisd.com and praisdcards.com returned No match (unregistered), and praisd.io returned Domain not found. Because the .com is newly held by an unrelated party, budget for a fallback domain.

An old abandoned 'Praisd' Flattr SDK on GitHub (https://github.com/dereulenspiegel/praisdsdk). No review-software or restaurant-tech conflict found.

candidates.name: Tabbl
candidates.rationale: Table plus tab (the check), with the vowel dropped so it is ownable. Five letters, instantly restaurant-flavored, and it names the exact moment the card gets dropped: with the tab, on the table. Verisign WHOIS on 2026-09-04: tabbl.com registered 2020 and returned no response when fetched (likely parked), while gettabbl.com and tabblcards.com returned No match (unregistered) and tabbl.io returned Domain not found. No company named Tabbl found in checks. Minor risk: some people will type Tabble or Table.

candidates.name: Bravi
candidates.rationale: Italian plural of bravo, used when applauding a whole cast - which is exactly what a good review does for the entire front and back of house. Five letters, universally pronounceable, and feels at home in Italian, American, and fine-dining contexts. Verisign WHOIS on 2026-09-04: bravi.com registered since 1999 (served no title when fetched), but getbravi.com and bravicards.com both returned No match (unregistered). bravi.io registered 2025-06-27 per whois.nic.io. No review or NFC company found under the name.

Bravi.app is a well-funded SMB-focused AI startup, likely to expand and to defend the name.

candidates.name: Encor
candidates.rationale: Encore without the E: what a guest asks for after a great show, and what a five-star review earns the restaurant (guests coming back). Five letters, reads clean, and it can double as the name of the monthly report ("your Encor report"). Collision note: encor.com (registered 1998) is Encor International, an unrelated company (page title fetched 2026-09-04). getencor.com and encorcards.com returned No match (unregistered) and encor.io returned Domain not found, per registry WHOIS on 2026-09-04. Trademark search needed given how common Encore-derived marks are.

Bing auto-corrects to 'encore'. All three checked domains are available, but encor.com not checked.

Eight letters, two syllables, and a server saying "drop the Chefkiss card" sounds natural. The logo practically designs itself. One word, two syllables, instantly understood by any server ('drop the Aftermint'). Reads cleanly on a card above 'Tap to review'. candidates.name: Last Course
